corpus_intended_use: Preregistered public development corpus for the Codex-only three-arm comparison. It asks again whether the full reviewer workflow beats the pattern catalog alone, on cases written after the severity-exception wording was added to the skill, and whether documented severity exceptions are applied on cases no model has seen. It is not sealed and does not establish generalization.
corpus_contamination_risk: The corpus is inspectable and was written by the same author who wrote the reviewer references it exercises. It was designed from the reference contracts alone, without reading any v9 run report. Every result must disclose that exposure and remain development evidence.

scoring.source_rendering_contract: Each embedded source line is prefixed with its 1-based number, right-aligned to six columns, and a tab, as `nl -ba` prints it. The prefix is display-only; findings must cite that number as `line`.
scoring.label_semantics_contract: Findings still match exact (pattern_id, severity, file, line) tuples. A finding label matches when a report hits its primary tuple or any accepted_alternatives tuple, and counts as one true positive however many of those tuples are reported. An optional label is excluded from true-positive and false-negative denominators; a report matching it is not a false positive and is counted separately as an optional match. fp_guard labels keep their meaning.
scoring.stability_contract: A finding or optional label is stable when the number of successful repetitions that matched any of its tuples meets the strict-majority rule. A stable prediction is a false positive only when it matches no finding or optional label tuple.

schedule.freeze_policy: Freeze sources, labels, and protocol before the first measured run. Any later edit creates a new version.
schedule.design_disclosure: Reviewer holdout v14 is v13 plus one preregistered output-normalization rule. V13 ran Claude claude-sonnet-5 on the frozen v10 corpus with the v11 infrastructure-retry policy and usage capture, and judged every answer with the strict single-JSON-payload parser. claude-sonnet-5 often wrapped its answer in one Markdown code fence (```json ... ```); the strict parser rejects that, the retry policy re-invoked the call once, and the model fenced its answer again, so 6 of 150 full-arm calls and 21 of 150 catalog-only calls ended unscoreable. No arm may have unscoreable runs, so v13 was stopped or finished without a counted result: no v13 skill-lift result is claimed, and v13's results are described separately in its own record. The output_normalization rule was fixed in this protocol before any v14 call. An answer that, after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, is exactly one fenced block, whose opening line is three backticks with an optional json info string and whose closing line is three backticks at the end, has its fences removed, and the text between them goes to the unchanged strict parser. Prose before or after a fence, two fenced blocks, a fence without a closing line, or a fence around non-JSON is judged by the strict parser as before. The rule applies identically to every arm (full, catalog-only, and no-skill); each run records output_normalized, and each report and the arm comparison count normalized runs per arm. It recovers no other malformed output and changes no finding, label, or scoring rule, and v13's reports are not rescored under it. Everything else is v13's: the single Claude host claude-sonnet-5 at the Claude Code 2.1.281 floor with claude_permission_mode off, usage capture, the infrastructure-retry policy unchanged (a scoreable output is never retried), the frozen v10 corpus reused unchanged by path and digest (30 cases, 15 Playwright, 15 Cypress), and the v10 arms, thresholds, seed, strict-majority stability rule, numbered sources, scoring contract, and five repetitions. The corpus is public development evidence that was inspected while designing v10, and its labels and the v10 attempt reports are public; it is not sealed and does not establish generalization. It is not a fresh-corpus test for the author: it already ran on Claude claude-opus-5 (v10), partly on Codex gpt-5.6-sol (the stopped v11 run), on Codex gpt-6-sol (v12), and on claude-sonnet-5 under v13; those runs do not train models. Results are not comparable across hosts with v10, v11, or v12; the full versus catalog-only and skill versus no-skill questions are answered within this one host. Usage is descriptive cost evidence only and enters no threshold or decision.

execution_identity.run_identity_capture: Capture the resolved runner path and CLI version in each report. Do not pin user-specific absolute paths or binary digests in this public protocol.
execution_identity.attestation_limit: Reported execution identity is provenance, not cryptographic attestation.

infrastructure_retry.contract: A scheduled call whose attempt times out, exits non-zero with a CLI usage, weekly, or rate limit message, or exits zero with output that is not one strict JSON payload is re-invoked in a freshly prepared identical workspace at the same schedule position, up to max_attempts_per_call attempts. Every attempt is recorded with its number, reason, and exit code. The final attempt is the one scored; an unscoreable final attempt stays an infrastructure error. A scoreable output is never retried, whatever its findings.

output_normalization.contract: Before the strict single-JSON-payload parser judges a model answer, the answer is trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace. If the trimmed answer is exactly one fenced block, whose first line is three backticks optionally followed by json, whose last line is three backticks, whose lines are separated by LF, and whose text between the fences contains no other run of three backticks, the text between the fences is passed to the strict parser unchanged. Any other answer, including prose before or after a fence, two fenced blocks, a fence without a closing line, or a fence around non-JSON, is judged by the strict parser as before. Each run records output_normalized, each report counts normalized runs, and the rule applies identically to every arm.

prompt_arms.matrix_requirement: Run a separate complete host matrix for full, catalog-only, and no-skill.

arm_comparison.temporal_validity_limit: Reported start/completion timestamps, fixed order, non-overlap, and a 12-hour first-start-to-last-completion window reduce arm-position and time-drift confounding but do not cryptographically attest time or identify or freeze provider backend revisions.

uncertainty.interpretation_limit: Bootstrap intervals describe case-resampling sensitivity on this fixed public case set. They do not quantify model-run stochasticity and are not population confidence intervals, independent replications, or release-grade causal inference.

decision.failure_semantics: Every threshold must pass against each control. A complete matrix that misses any threshold is FAIL, not partial evidence.

claim_policy.pass: Development skill-lift evidence is limited to this fixed public corpus, declared model identifiers, captured CLI versions, prompts, and schedule; provider backend snapshots are not attested.
claim_policy.partial_results: Descriptive arm metrics may be published, but never as a causal or partial skill-lift claim.

decision.point_estimate_limits: Threshold crossings on this small fixed public development corpus are descriptive signals. The corpus is public and inspectable. Confidence intervals accompany point estimates; sealing, independent blind evaluation after publication, cryptographic runner attestation, cross-provider replication, and population-level generalization are not established.

cross_host_decision.aggregation_intent: Single-host Claude protocol; the single declared host is evaluated directly and no cross-provider claim is allowed.

evidence_limitations.message: prompt-complete zero-tool execution stages parent authentication material, not a disposable scoped credential; this report is development evidence and is not release-eligible
